He entered the room, placed a bamboo comb across the desk, and said, "In the kingdom of Magadha, this decree was personally issued by the King himself.

Facing the wall for nine years, he passed the ladder with the bandits; thus, these extraordinary circumstances met an extraordinary person to inspire him.

This most sublime great matter must be proclaimed in a most sublime place. A single phrase that strikes the mark causes the sound of bells, drums, wooden clappers, and fish-bells to shake heaven and earth;
a thousand chariots follow the same track, regardless of whether one is a learner (*śaikṣa*) or beyond learning (*aśaikṣa*).
Studying the profound mystery, we join hands and return to the same source. We draw from the final currents of the Suishui Commentary and receive the lingering moisture of Caoxi.
If one proceeds in this manner, there is no need for a new "sage. To further illustrate, let us cite Śākyamuni, Yuanhe, and Buddhatrāta—aha ha!
Let us all together sing the song of Great Peace.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said: "Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra discourse extensively on principle and phenomena; Deshan and Linji employ only the staff and the shout.
Do you all know the application of Xingxing? [He] threw down his staff and said: 'Though it be a dead snake, if one knows how to handle it, it comes alive.'"
Ascending the hall, he said: "There is nothing that does not meet the eye; what do you say when the moment arrives? The coin is of full value; the goods are at their set price.
Having worn through seven cushions of *pūtanga* grass, one sees the whole world only upon rolling up the curtain. To pursue the wind from a thousand miles away is not the mark of a swift horse."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Huangbo striking Linji—this is a sign of an abundant harvest. Xinghua chasing Kebin—the shrimp bends for its offspring.
Their merit covers the age, yet it must be weighed anew. A single furnace casts a golden ball; struck from the tip of the staff, a jade qilin emerges."
Ascending the hall, he took up his staff and called to the assembly, saying: "Deshan used this to scatter flying sparks;
Zhaozhou used this to climb the mountain and beat the dog; Xingsheng used this to prop open the door and support the threshold; and monks use this to cross waters and pierce through clouds."
If you call this the staff, you will enter hell as swiftly as a shot arrow. [The Master] planted the staff and descended from the seat.
Entering the hall, he was pure and naked, bright and clear—graceful amidst the willows and flowers, appearing faintly before the wind and beneath the moon.
He struck the meditation platform once and said: "The marvelous brushstrokes of Monk You are difficult to depict.

On the tenth day of the second month, having returned from a mountain excursion, he ascended the hall and spoke, citing how one day Changsha, upon returning from a mountain excursion, arrived at the gate.
The Head Seat asked, "Where have you come from, Master? The Monk said, "I have come from wandering the mountains. The Head Seat asked, "From where did you arrive?
The Monk said, "At first I followed the fragrant grasses away; then I returned, chasing the falling flowers. The Head Seat said, "That is very much like the spirit of spring.
The Monk said, "It is even better than autumn dew dripping upon lotuses. The Verse says: [Blank] ... the principle of the shuttle and loom. Pervasive...
In the gardens they weave fine silks; only the yellow oriole understands this intent. Hardly has it cast a furtive glance when spring has already passed.
[The Master] ascended the hall and raised the case of Muzhou Daowu and Yangshan Huiji while picking tea. Muzhou said, "All day long I have heard only your voice, but I do not see your form.
Yangshan then shook the tea tree. Muzhou said, "You have attained its function, but you have not attained its essence. Yangshan...
Yangshan asked, "What about you, Master? Miaoyan remained silent for a long time. Yangshan said, "Master, you have attained the essence, but you have not attained the function.
Miaoyan said, "I grant you thirty blows! [The Commentator] says: When the wind does not blow, the tree does not move. This concerns the father and son, Miaoyan and Yangshan.

Body and function are presented to one another. The story of the thirty blows from the staff has already been put into practice; ten thousand oxen turn their heads back, for the mountain and the earth are heavy.

At the summer retreat’s small *can*, he strikes once with the master’s staff and says: "Throughout the entire body there is no shadow or image; pervading the entire world, it is free from all obstruction.
It tears asunder the past and present, manifesting a standard that is already established. Yet, it was forcibly met with many expedient doors by Śākyamuni the Old Man. Long...

During the ninety days of summer retreat, even a rooster was forced to lay eggs; this may be called the re-arising of images where no images existed, or the re-establishment of barriers where all barriers had ceased.
Since it is said that one takes Perfect Enlightenment as the monastery (*ārāma*), where is there that is not a place for the summer retreat?
When one regards worldly toil as entirely one's own self, what living beings are there to protect? Thus, one knows that the fundamental nature is pure.
However, the names and characteristics that serve as the causes for defilement are interpenetrating and unimpeded; they remain embedded within one's practice.

Within the school of the patch-robed monks (śramaṇas), even to speak of them is entirely unacceptable. Since we of our own kind eat the Buddha’s food and wear the Buddha’s robes, we must not entirely claim that the Buddha was wrong, nor hastily alter the Buddha’s regulations.
When the holy arises, let us follow the error with the error. This very topic—how is it that people nowadays merely act?

When walking, do not tread upon the ancient imperial road. When standing, simply stand; do not linger by the green of exotic grasses. When sitting, simply sit; do not lean against the edge of the Black Mountain.
When lying down, simply lie down; do not settle upon pure ground. Why? Although Chang’an is pleasant, it is not a place for long-term residence.

Again, it is recounted: During a night session at Dongshan, the lamp was not lit. After a monk had finished his discourse and retired, Dongshan ordered an attendant to light the lamp and call the monk who had just spoken forward.
As the monk approached, Dongshan told him to take some flour—two or three *liang*—and gave it to him.
The monk shook out his sleeves and withdrew. Thereupon, he attained realization. The monk then exhausted his clothing and funds to provide a vegetarian feast. Three years later, however...

He came to take his leave of Dongshan. Dongshan said, "Farewell. At that time, Xuefeng was standing in attendance and asked, "As for this monk who has just departed, how long will it be before he returns?
Dongshan replied, "He only knows one [thing], yet he comes. That monk returned to his quarters and passed away beneath his bedding.
When the news was reported to Dongshan, Dongshan said, "He is still three lifetimes ahead of me. [The Master] commented: "..."
Dongshan’s exchange with this monk was like drawing out silk and weaving thread; it was dense and subtle, worthy of close observation.
Yet, once he was pressed by Xuefeng, the needle-point was suddenly exposed. Even so, as for passing away while still wearing his robes, why did he still fall short of me by three lifetimes?
Do you understand? The shrimp bends for its offspring.
At Lingyin, in the quarters of the front hall, during the summer retreat, the whisk was held (after retiring from Xingsheng).
To summarize the essential points: Before Lingyin and behind Tianzhu, it is as level as a mirror’s surface yet as precipitous as a cliff. Beneath the single robe lies the pickaxe.
It cannot be rolled into a ball, nor can it be torn apart. It is truly laughable that Tripitaka Master Huiri’s perspective was so erroneous;
he stubbornly pointed to a peak right before him and claimed it had come from Vulture Peak. This is what is called "shooting at a stone tiger in Lantian and mistakenly killing General Li."
Little do they realize that before the world was manifested, it stood solitary and towering; though mist and clouds may change, its deep azure remains eternally concentrated.
To realize the proof within the three periods does not exceed this; for the summer retreat of nine months, one relies entirely upon this very thing. [The Master] drew a line across the air and said:
"Furthermore, regarding the phrase 'Smell the earth and know the opportunity,' how would you say it? When the wind is fierce, the dragon follows."
At the bottom of the pool, the moon rises high as a monkey emerges from its cave-dwelling and chants.
Last night, the Abbot of Fangzhang raised the public case concerning Layman Langya’s instruction to the assembly, saying:
"All of you who have come here to spend the summer retreat with me—I shall point out for you five kinds of illnesses. He then added: "The Elder of Langya was compassionate..."
Indeed. Among the four hundred and four ailments, five types of illness have been singled out for humanity; these may be called medicines that cause dizziness and nausea.

Nevertheless, when one examines the matter closely, even if these five illnesses were suddenly eliminated, what would one do if the dietary taboos associated with the medicine had not yet been forgotten?
"Set aside the medicinal taboos; bring forth a single phrase! [The Master] gives a shout. The Teacher comments: "To point out the source of the illness—Langya is indeed intimate.
To set aside the medicinal taboos—the Head of the Hall is thoroughly exhausted in his grandmotherly concern.

When one enters the gate of a physician, the patient's condition becomes even worse. Among them, there may be those who can be treated; for such, it is not improper to administer this one pill. [He strikes with his whisk.]
Tapping the corner of the meditation platform once, he said: "Watch your diet!
Watch your diet! Compiled by the Dharma-heirs Zhengcong, Miaoen, and others from Nengren Chan Monastery at Mount Yan in Wenzhou.

Entering through the three gates, he addressed the assembly, saying: "Before a single thought arises, one has already roamed throughout the Flower Treasury World; before the feet have even been set down, one has already transcended Vairocana.
If you say that a single dharma exists outside the gate, you will laugh Vimalakīrti into a state of collapse."
In the Buddha Hall: "Dust away the dust to see the Buddha; yet the Buddha is also dust. This mountain monk uses his foot-cloth as a kitchen towel; not seeing with the eyes is purity.

After ascending the seat and offering prayers for the Emperor (the *zhusheng*), [the questions and answers are not recorded]. He then said: "The Dharma has no fixed characteristics; to conceive of it is to deviate from it. The Way..."
The distant man stands out yet is difficult to discern; he is like the clouds parting over Yandang Mountain, where wondrous peaks and strange rocks are scattered like stars across the landscape.
It is also like a waterfall cascading from Longjiu, where amidst the bright sun and blue sky, thunder roars and rain pours down, often striking one spot while missing another.

People often listen to oral traditions merely for the sake of hearsay; even when they arrive at the truth, it remains unilluminated. Most especially, they interpret this as a mere present-conditioned state.

If one does not interpret it as a conditioned state, then there is something worth discussing: the opening of the eye of wisdom upon the heads of the thousand sages, and the manifestation of a jade tower upon a single blade of grass.
Thank you both for ascending the hall. With meager merit, I dwell at Changyun; my life’s work is simply to follow the truth.
The lantern hangs from the pillar; the Big Dipper faces the Southern Dipper. Every dharma rests in its proper place; every function meets the person. Let us all exert our efforts together.
He helped up a broken sand-pitcher. Ascending the hall, he said:
"Siddhārtha sticks his head out and flaunts his ugly behavior; Yunmen could not strike him dead, and Deshan could not scold him into silence.
In the morning, one listens to the orioles singing in the garden; the Vairambha wind of old is just as it is today. He struck the floor with his staff.
It is said: "If you can realize it at this moment, you will together realize the Tathāgata’s pure Dharma-body.
If it is otherwise, you have merely wasted a ladleful of water in a stagnant pool."

A Small Sermon for the Summer Retreat: Before the differentiation of sentient beings and Buddhas, there was a state utterly transcending the marks of coming and going. As soon as form and name first appeared, the occasion for "untying knots" arose.
One establishes a monastery of Perfect Enlightenment and breaks the rice-pot lid; one speaks of the Wisdom of Equality and turns the bowl upside down.
Bringing it all out from the very bottom, it has been scattered and cleared away. This is precisely the time, within these ninety days and throughout the twelve periods of the day and night.
He painted the clouds of Mount Yan to their end and fully enjoyed the moon over Dragon Pool. Even though it is so, I must still ask you:
when Changyun Peak and Cariren Peak compete for the forehead, which is the [numbered] turn? He answered on their behalf: "Seven down, eight down."
Master Xie presided over the opening ceremony of the summer retreat at Du Temple and ascended the hall. "Although this humble temple is desolate, the striking of the hour does not fail its time.

Just look at the formal commencement of the retreat yesterday; everything was largely in accordance with established custom. As for whether the eyebrows are long or short, that remains yet to be asked."
He clenched his hand into a fist and said, "A steamed bun this large—how many can one person eat?
After a long silence, he said, "No one understands this meaning; it makes me remember Yangqi."

A small-scale *sǎn* (sermon) for the end of the summer retreat: A single word exhausts the Way; it is as hard as a wax man or ice. A single stroke meets the critical moment; it is as soft as an iron bullet.
It is perfectly round without seams or gaps; it is elusive and beyond all names or forms. Even the Three Sages and Ten Holy Ones cannot fathom this school.

From the Eastern Land to the Western Heaven—who can clarify this principle? Even if one has deeply realized it and possesses constant, clear knowledge, what is this that is manifest as the absolute reality?
[The Master] strikes the ground once with his staff and says: "I and you have failed to understand this exchange of question and answer."
Meeting, one only understands that *nasiqi*. Again, it is cited:
A monk asked Yunmen, "What is it like when the trees are stripped of their leaves? Yunmen said, "The body is exposed in the golden wind.
[The Master] comments: Old Man Yunmen—his three phrases can be discerned. One arrow pierces the vast sky; before you even raise your eyebrows, you have already missed.
[The Master] passes through. The Capable One (Śākyamuni) uses one arrowhead to break another arrowhead; everyone, look with an urgent eye! He strikes the meditation staff once and says, "Middle.
[He then] ascends the hall to collect debts. When the three rounds of drums have ceased, they crowd upward together. Stepping forward, they are like those demanding payment of a debt.
If we speak of collecting debts, recently Supervisor Zhang and Patrol Leader Li have emptied the granaries and exhausted the storehouses.
What "manure pits" do you have left for me? There is no need to exhaust yourself with such bitter pressure or to clamor in hunger. Just listen to your brother-in-law;
he will turn nothing into something and provide a separate allocation. (He taps the table once. "The mouse-teeth grains of the earth—every single grain is like a treasure. A tip!
The measure cannot be exhausted; it requires only two equal divisions. Striking the sounding block twice, he ascends the hall on the fifteenth day of the tenth month.
In the deep ravine, cold waves surge; upon the frost-covered trees, the leaves drift away. This is an event from the distant era of the Putong year.
Vividly present this very day. [End of] Session.
Small *saman* on the Winter Solstice: To fully raise or partially raise [the teaching] is to drive a stake into empty space; to speak horizontally or vertically is to plant flowers upon a stone.
Holding up his staff, he said: "This very single peak of the Heavenly Pillar—until now, no one has spoken of it.
If you can speak of it, then you shall see the icy river burst into flame and the iron trees bloom with flowers. If not, it turns instead into the Banner-Displaying Peak."

Although these great elders had eyes that transcended their schools and reached upward while connecting downward, compared to one who awakens spontaneously without a teacher, the distance between them is as vast as heaven and earth.
Therefore, regarding the single pivot of the ultimate, the sages do not transmit it; were one to conceive a thought or stir a notion, there would be no interval at all.
“Incorrect. You do not yet know what the divine light of Kāśyapa illuminates; you merely smile with a faint grin and silently seize upon the opportunity.
Though you may thus see through the fundamental tenets, you are still merely leaning against the gate or standing by the door.
If you wish for clouds to rise from the Southern Mountain and rain to fall on the Northern Mountain, you must recognize that the tiger has always been the tiger.”

The following day, the Princess ascended the hall of the ancestral shrine. The Great Perfection has no interior, dissolving all darkness; its wondrous responsiveness knows no fixed direction, emptily encompassing the ten thousand phenomena.
It emerges and submerges within the ocean of precious luminous space; it roams freely through the twelve jade towers. One name for it is the Boundless Body (*Anantakāya*);
another is the Land of Secret Adornment (*Ghanavyūha*). Whether casting off life or entering a new birth, this is the enjoyment [of the Buddhas]. Only Buddha and Buddha [can fully realize it].
Only then can one know it. When this fundamental matter is known, all doubt and suspicion cease. Here and there is Maitreya; no gate, no Sudhana. Ascending the hall, he said:
"In the second month, spring is nearly half-way through; the peach blossoms are in full bloom. Since Lingyun departed, to whose house have the fragrant petals fallen?
As for the saying, 'To this very day, I have no further doubts'—what is it that they do not doubt? When encountering rice, they eat."
[The Master] ate rice. When he encountered tea, he drank the tea.

On the first day of the third month, he ascended the hall to express his gratitude to the late Reverend Banruo Baitang. "The spring days are long and leisurely; the spring flowers are in full, radiant bloom.
The numinous light of Prajñā is manifest and uninterrupted. Holding up his whisk, he said, "Do you see? Striking the meditation seat with his staff, he said, "It cannot be grasped."
Gathered together, they cannot be dispersed.
Upon the commencement of the retreat, he ascends the hall: one direct path and two circumlocutions; not following old precedents, he establishes a distinct way of life.
Performing somersaults within the hollow of a lotus fiber, he catches shrimp amidst the surging waves of the wheat fields.

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The sun and moon are like shuttlecocks; time passes like an arrow. Before one's eyes, a single pivot undergoes ten thousand transformations and a thousand changes.
Where can this be seen? [He struck the floor with his staff. A gust of west wind arrives, and two or three leaves fall."
The late Master Túnguìng’s letter has arrived; I ascend the hall to address you. Within the ranks of Lingxiao, we once shared the same fires and divided the spoils.
Before the Xiao Duo Peak, the skillful merchant never stops his trade in dead stock. Casting one's body across to the other shore, even the hawk’s eye loses its track.
Returning to the root, one deeply attains the essential meaning; fallen leaves dance in the western wind.
Ascending the hall on the anniversary of Bodhidharma’s passing: One foot spans the Western Heavens; a single sandal remains in the Eastern Land.
That toothless old barbarian has always walked with wide strides. His descendants search everywhere across the earth for traces of his origins.

I long remember the fifth day of the tenth month every year. Raising his staff, he asked: "Do you see the Patriarch? Striking the ground with the staff, he said: "Aaaah! The wild geese cry out amidst the clouds."
The piercing frost wind assails the doors; we return to the new Sangha Hall.
Master Xie Pingzhang, Duke Guo, ascends the hall. How extraordinary! How extraordinary! The peaks of Huading on Mount Tiantai are magnificent;
directly below is directly below! The stone bridge of Mount Nanyue is high. It upholds that which the Buddhas and Patriarchs have not transmitted. Support it! Support it!

Heaven and Earth are revealed in their solitary majesty. He takes up his staff and strikes it on the left side, saying: "If you understand this side, it is like the sun shining across the sky. He strikes it on the right side, saying:
"If you see clearly within this, it is like water rushing toward a valley. By means of this, he sweeps away all obstacles; by means of this, he accomplishes the two kinds of adornment;
by means of this, he brings peace to the three borders; by means of this, he governs the common people. He distributes precious delicacies...

Fragrant Accumulation: To pin Mount Wondrous Joy upon the point of a needle—when great function manifests before one, where does the merit reside? A thousand-year-old crane perches on the pine as the moonlight grows cold;
a man of half-leisure faces the brightness of the bamboo window.
Ascending the hall: The drum has been struck; the incense has been burned. All of you should see it right now: this is the season of the Great Cold.
To wait for the old monk to wag his three-inch tongue would surely be like adding frost to snow.
Giving thanks to the former Head Monk and addressing the assembly of old acquaintances, he ascended the hall and said: "A forest of sandalwood is surrounded by sandalwood;
a forest of thorns is surrounded by thorns. A forest of thorns may be surrounded by sandalwood; a forest of sandalwood may be surrounded by thorns."
One who penetrates these four layers of barriers may be granted the status of a true, fundamental monk. But tell me, who can penetrate them?
Faceless, with dark, weathered, and wrinkled skin; he bursts through the moon atop Mount Huading and tramples the clouds upon the Stone Bridge. (He plants his staff.)
When Master Xie Shipuo visited, he ascended the hall and said: "The mountains of Wu are green, the mountains of Yue are green. In yielding and deference, host and guest are distinguished;

in rising and falling, brothers are revealed. As for that single phrase in between—wind stilled, tide calm—the entire assembly are Gu and Lu; though they grasp their brushes, it is difficult to complete the painting."

Upon newly assuming the position of the Abbot of Tianshi Monastery, the Reverend ascended the hall. Holding up his staff, he said: "The clouds of consecration have dispersed; the moon over Mount Emei shines in broad daylight.
Father and son share one and the same heart, forged as if from solid cast iron. The younger responds to the elder’s call; the entire mechanism is revealed.
But tell me, what is it that is revealed? Water chestnuts from Suzhou; lotus roots from Shao Bo. He then struck the ground with his staff.

Ascending the hall, he said: "The spring mountains layer upon layer of chaotic green; the spring waters are limpid and azure. The gates of the pavilions stand wide open, and the body manifests in thousands of millions of forms.
A single thought of deviation, and the clouds roll in thickly; Sudhana has no way to seek out his spiritual friends."
The Buddha’s Birthday: Ascending the Hall. Emerging from his mother’s womb, he darkened the seas and mountains; Pointing to heaven and pointing to earth, as if there were no one else.
Year after year, all the waters of West Lake are poured forth, Yet they cannot wash away the dust that covers Śākyamuni’s face.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "It is not mind, nor is it Buddha. The jade hare rises in the east; the golden crow sets in the west.
Circulating without a moment's pause, in the end, what thing is it? Which man possesses such strength of arm as to strike the cave of the spirit through with a single blow?"
The Master struck the sounding block once.
On the eighth day of the twelfth month, he ascended the hall and said: "How high is the Snowy Mountain? It stands towering above the heavens. Alas for the Sage of India!

For six years he could not reach its summit. But when he finally reached it, all paths were cut off. With his back turned, he plucked the Southern Dipper; looking down, he saw that all other peaks were but small."
A Tribute to Chan Master Mu of Chengtian Monastery in Quanzhou, and the Opening Address at Fashi. Holding up his staff, he struck it once and said:
"Fashi preaches the Dharma. He struck it again and said: "He does not speak of Chan. Every word contains the wondrous; its clarity does not reside in speech."

It is difficult to hear with the ears; it is valued only in its transmission through the mind. Apart from this, do not seek other mystical paths to enter. From the bridge in Luoyang, one gazes toward Chang’an.
On the day of the Buddha’s birth, he descended from his mother’s womb with a resolve as vast as a bushel, yet he first learned the ways of a small child.
He then let out a lion’s roar; with water in his lake and the ladle in his hand, he seized the moment to sweep it all away into non-existence.
This is even superior to the old "ancient spike" Yunmen. An empty medicine bag dangles behind a funeral carriage.

Small Sermon for the Summer Retreat. Holding up his staff, he said: "The life-force of the patch-robed monks and the governing principles of the ancestral community—both holding fast and letting go depend entirely upon this.
Laying the staff across horizontally, he said: "As for holding fast, the green mountains dare not be green, and the white clouds dare not be white;
it is as if a cloth bag were tied with a single knot, leaving no opening for either sage or ordinary person to breathe. Striking the ground with the staff, he said: "If..."
The treatise permits both letting go and proceeding. Deep caves resound with the music of flowing water; clear lakes are layered with lotus coins.

These are all sites for the *Candālī* monastery (*Caṅgalama*), perfectly suitable for dwelling and making use of. Yet, as for "neither grasping firmly nor letting go"—how is this one phrase to be understood?
Leaning on his staff, he said: "Only the cuckoo knows this meaning; Its cries pierce through the moonlight of the third watch."
Again, he cites Huangbo’s question to Baizhang: "How do you instruct others regarding the ancestral vehicle? Baizhang remained seated. Huangbo asked, "How will future descendants transmit it?
Baizhang said, "I thought you were a man of substance," and then returned to his quarters.
[The Master] comments: Huangbo stepped forward with determination; he did not shrink from losing face. Xiong峰 (Xiongpeng) was fond of forgetting his own shame and was willing [to acknowledge this].
Looking on the side, although he immediately patched it over, in the end it was difficult to deceive the eyes of the multitude. How is this known?
A lion teaches its cub the secret of bewildering its offspring; as soon as [the cub] intends to leap forward, it has already turned its body.
Ascending the hall to open the Treasury of Eternal Life with the Chief Administrator and the Rector: The ancestral rules of Yangqi are solemn and strict;
no one has raised dissent. Xinghua’s staff was stern and unyielding; misfortune does not come alone. Borrowing the ladder and steps of these two elders, he opens the storehouse of the One Vehicle.
Raising his fly-whisk, he said: "The plum rains have passed and the bamboo breeze is cool; the lake light is vast and shimmering, the lotus fragrance wafts."
"Ha! What a great mess!
On the first day of the eighth month, the Secretary and the Hall Master take their leave. Going east, going west; coming from the south, coming from the north.
Copper heads and iron jaws; horse faces and donkey muzzles. They leap and bound upon the tip of a hair; they dance the *Santai* within the shadow of the lamp. Yanfu [Temple]."
Let us first establish a semblance; it must be well done so that one may see it clearly for oneself. Master Zhuo said: "With eyes blurred by sleep, they cannot be opened.
On the first day of the ninth month, he ascended the hall. Monks rushed forward to gaze upon him. Gaze, but do not fail this gazing; when drinking water, one must value its source.
The Master of the Gate, Fuben, at the time of greeting and at the tea station, opened a living path for all people.
If it had been Xie Sanlang, he would have simply raised his eyebrows and departed. [The Master] strikes the staff.
To the Dharma Family: Former Master Yishan Wuye ascends the hall. He cites the public case where Yishan asked Shuangfeng, "Brother disciple, how is your realization these days?
[The Master] comments: To study with a teacher is not as good as studying with a friend; Yishan and Shuangfeng were truly superior in this regard.
They simply failed to establish the distinction between subject and object through the division of knowledge and views. Today, Elder Brother Yishan—if...
Question: When it comes to the perspective of Manifesting Blessings (Yanfu), one reaches a point where there are no words with which to respond and no principles by which to argue.
Nevertheless, this still does not avoid leaving the entire world in a state of doubt.
Ascending the hall for the Lantern Festival, he addressed the assembly, saying: "The house to the east lights its lanterns; the house to the west sits in darkness.
It is the same Lantern Festival, yet each pursues their own livelihood. Those who sit in darkness silently bring forth mindfulness; those who light the lanterns clearly illuminate everything.
What is it that is illuminated? [He raises his staff and strikes once. The horse from Haitan is as large as a donkey."
The Record of the Zen Master of Longxiang Xingqing Chan Temple at Jiangxin, Wenzhou, Compiled by His Dharma Heirs Shoujing, Miaoen, and Others. According to the Abbot:
"Perfectly clear, there are no words. A fist suddenly strikes the chest. The waters of the Shen River run swift; no boats are permitted to moor."
He held up the official decree and said: "The pivot of the great transformation, the central pillar of the turbulent current—now returned to my grasp, its application shall be seen.
But what of it when one encounters a time of wild waves? He then said: "Decree! (Zha).

General Outline: Practicing the Dharma in accordance with the Dharma, the banner of the Dharma is established wherever one goes. Yesterday, while residing at Yanfu, I knew only the gates of the Dharma within the mountains:

the music of the waters was tumultuous and the wind through the bamboos played in succession; the empty valley echoed the resonance of the golden bell, and the sparse forest carried the songs of woodcutters.
Today, having arrived at Longxiang, I behold once more the scenery upon the river: the ripples of the waves undulate, and the misty boats...
Intersecting and crisscrossing, the watchtowers broadcast the sound of painted horns; with favorable winds, the fishermen’s songs are passed along.
Although the streams and mountains differ, the clouds and moon are ultimately the same. Mind, Buddha, and sentient beings—these three are without distinction.
At this very moment, Bodhisattva Lingzhao comes forth and says: "Three thousand years, and the Yellow River clears once."
That evening’s informal discourse: Waving a hand across the river is only fit for catching shrimp; brandishing oars and displaying paddles is not fit for feeding a dog.
Even if one has a surplus of fragrant bait and casts a ten-thousand-mile hook, or passes through the deep seas and spreads a net that covers the heavens—what can be done?
Though one sets one's heart on great things, one stumbles upon a cold water and a quiet night, where the moon is bright and the boat returns empty-handed. Therefore, this mountain monk says:
Arriving here, not a single wave has stirred; not even a shred of armor or a tiny scale remains. Let things be as they are. Why?
To catch fish from deep waters, one must have long since surrendered to fate; he has never offered wine to the River God.
Again, he cites Zhaozhou’s late-evening instruction: "Tonight, I shall answer questions. Let anyone who can ask a question come forward.
At that time, a monk came out and bowed. Zhaozhou said, "This time I have thrown a brick only to draw out a jade; yet I have drawn out nothing but a mere brick. Commentary:
Gold is tested by stone, jade by fire, and a person by their words. This monk had not yet opened his mouth [when Zhaozhou spoke].
"The Way is this very brick. Why is that? If one does not pay the price, how can one distinguish the true from the false?
On the following day, he ascended the seat in the High Hall and said: "When the myriad things are taken as oneself, where is there 'self' and 'other'? When the four seas are taken as one's home,"
How can one distinguish its boundaries? The moon over the Yangtze River opens wide the golden gates; the wind through the pines perpetually proclaims the jade-like tones.

Veneration is proclaimed everywhere; the wondrous is manifested at every turn. The measure of the Sage is extinguished, transcending the Buddha-lands; the waves of grace flow forth, blessing the imperial domain.
Closing the session: Recalling the immortal’s journey, his carriage has not yet returned; I specially offer my loyal devotion to raise the wind-banners.
I pull open the golden locks of the Jade Palace, yet I most dread directly confronting the Sage’s countenance.

Thank you, both classes, for ascending the hall. On the mountain above the Yangtze River lies a mountain temple; its gate opens facing the capital city. The two orders, east and west, must not be disturbed. Why?
Because "The Dharma abides in the station of the Dharma; the characteristics of the world are eternally constant."
Ascending the hall on the Double Fifth: Today is the fifth day of the fifth month. Seize this moment to utter a single phrase:
there are no mountains from which to gather medicinal herbs, yet there is water sufficient for a dragon boat race. The river is as vast as this; the rowers assemble to steer it together.
Reaching neither the far shore nor dwelling upon this shore, they abide only in the midst of the current—abiding nowhere at all. Before the movement of the mind, they have seized the silken prize.
Returning home, the stone woman and wooden man vie with one another to dance.
Master Xie Ba’en visits his two Dharma brothers, Dou-shuai Xi-weng and Dong-geng, at the Hall; atop the Jizifeng Peak.
Clouds part and clouds gather; dragons soar above the river. The tide ebbs and the tide flows level. As for the matter of the Master’s lineage, it is perfectly clear and distinct.
Before the wind, there is no need to call out "elder brother"; after seeing [the truth], there is no need to respond "younger brother."
Ascending the hall, he raised the example of Master Zhengjue Yi, who said:

"I remember when I was seven years old, at a village school, I attained a Dharma gate that transcends emotion and leaves behind views—most wondrous and most profound. If you wish to uphold it, you should listen attentively.

After the high and thick fields have been plowed and sown, he returns home trailing his tablets and carrying firewood on his back; in the deep night, with a single brazier of fire, the whole family is present.

*Shangyi*. "Virtuous ones of the various dhyānas, when meeting people you must not speak erroneously. The Master said, "Yesterday, because of the snow, I could not help but cite the ancients and draw upon the present.
I recall that when I was three years old, still in my swaddling clothes, I received a wondrous principle:
to dismantle delusion and exhaust the source, it is neither empty nor existent. To clearly understand this definitive point, one must rely on the mind to hear it. Spring Snow."

Filling the sky, it comes; touching every place, it seems like flowers blooming. Not knowing which tree in the garden is the true plum—O venerable seniors, whenever you meet someone, simply raise this point in such a manner.
Ascending the hall at Nirvana Monastery, he patted his chest and told them; then he stretched out his legs to show them. There was a reason for this, yet there was no handle to grasp.
Two thousand years since the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, the bhikṣus have little sense of shame.

I, Xuefeng, request you to provide the essential outline. To erect the Dharma-banner and establish the fundamental tenet (zongzhi): having already received the Master’s instruction, one ought to attend to the official dispatch.
But how does one establish the fundamental tenet and the Dharma-banner? When the boat is launched, all share a single fate; only then do we station the Flying Tigers at the heart of the river.
When the drum is beaten to summon the three armies, we further deploy the Long Serpent across the Snowy Peaks. The realm is suddenly cleared, yet it still bears the traces of—
Jia. Only when the Mind-King beholds [it] directly do hostilities cease.
Compiled by the Dharma-heirs Cizheng and Miaoen from the *Recorded Sayings* of Chan Master Chongsheng of Xuefeng in Fuzhou.
Pointing to the three gates, he said: "The gate that has no gate—yet one must obtain the gate to enter. The intention that has no intention—yet one must grasp the intention to penetrate.
He snapped his fingers and asked: "Do you understand? One leaf to the west, one leaf to the east."
In the Buddha Hall, he burned incense, saying: "Raising my hand, I take up the incense; bowing my head, I pay homage. He declared, "I am the Dharma King; I am sovereign over the Dharma.
Taking his seat in the hall, he took up his staff and said: "By this, the dull and stubborn are melted away; by this, the partial and the limited are struck down. It is direct within the direct."
A curve within a curve; straightness within the curve. Old Lu did not understand it; Bodhidharma did not recognize it.
Holding up the official decree, he said: "A single decree at the head; no gasping for breath. The Great Balance casts forth all things; shifting the ground, spring is born."
The Buddhas and Patriarchs all come to hear the dispensation.

Grasping the essential principles, he casts down the mountain of the giant tortoise; winning the right to have his words circulate for a thousand ages. Holding up the "tortoise-nose" staff alone, one knows not how many have been wounded by it.
Now the balance rests with me; I must first root out their kind. Discerning them from beneath my eyes, I drag them forth.
Several instances. In one instance, he rolled amidst the reeds, his entire body crimson and raw. In another, he startled Śakra, his face covered in shame.
In another, he pierced through seven meditation cushions, his corpse lying across the road. In another, he entered the innermost city.

Turning the tail into the head, there is yet another strand that protrudes, difficult to distinguish. Looking over it again and again from every angle, it turns out to be nothing but a perennial rattan vine.
(He strikes the staff once.)

Again, it is recounted that Prime Minister Pei visited Shishuang. Shishuang snatched away the prime minister’s ceremonial tablet (hù) and asked, "In the hand of the Son of Heaven, it is called a *guī*;
in the hand of an official, it is called a *hù*. In the hands of this mountain monk, what do you call it? The Prime Minister was speechless, whereupon Shishuang kept the tablet for himself.
[The Master] comments: To call it a *guī* or a *hù* is to forcibly establish names and models. The Prime Minister understood the pivotal moment (*jī*).
He was unwilling to lightly leak [the secret] before others. Shishuang displayed his brilliance; gaining the advantage is losing the advantage.

That evening, during the small *sāman*, he said: "Beside the wheel of the sun and moon, shoulders are pressed together and feet are thrust in; beneath the lair of fish and dragons, knotted joints and coiled roots."
I know well that the ancestral style has been humbled; yet in right concentration, it is difficult to escape the transformative creation.
Rolling up to the summit of the Six-Flower Peak, one forces open the wondrous gate of the thousand sages. When discussing the moment of meeting, it is already eight *kē* too late.
Have you not heard the Way? "At Wàngzhōu Pavilion, I have met you. "At Wūshí Ridge, I have met you. "In front of the Sangha Hall, I have met you."
It is understood. Nevertheless, how could you know that the new Elder has long been in audience with all of you before he even crossed the Flying Crane Bridge?
After all, what do you take as your basis? Have you not heard it said: "A thousand miles is not yet far"?
Again, San-sheng raised the question to the Patriarch Chen-jo, saying, "A golden-scaled fish that has passed through the net—what does it eat?

The Patriarch said, "Wait until it emerges from the net, and then I will tell you. San-sheng said, "Of the fifteen hundred good spiritual friends [in this assembly], not even one recognizes the point of this dialogue.
Chen-jo said, "This old monk’s duties as abbot are too numerous. [The Commentator] says: If it were not for San-sheng, he would have been left hanging.
Head! Do not block the mouths of turtles and snakes. Were it not for the vast capacity of our Patriarch, how could he have tolerated scales that had already passed through the net?
To say, "The affairs of the abbot are many," is merely to be habitually clever at seizing every advantage.
A Small Sermon on New Year’s Eve: When one’s fields and gardens are secure and well-tended, how can one know that the path ahead is perilous?

When one sports with supernatural powers (*ṛddhi*), one turns the head away and pays no heed to the leaking roof. Yet when the year comes to its end and the cycle of time is exhausted, everyone finds their hands flustered and feet in a rush.
You must realize the self in order to understand what is before you; or is it by understanding what is before you that you realize the self? To attain both essence and function is like a carriage.
There is the wheel; both host and guest complete. It is like a bird with wings. Master Zhuang said: "Directly penetrating the blue sky, there is no obstruction;
pushing across the Great Way, one is entirely free."
Again, I cite Master Yaoshan’s night discourse, where he said: "I have a phrase; I will wait until a hornless ox gives birth to a calf before I tell it to you.
At that time, a monk stepped forward and said, "The hornless ox has given birth to a calf, yet the Master does not speak.
Yaoshan called to his attendant, "Bring a lamp! The monk then withdrew and joined the assembly. [The Commentator] remarks: Yaoshan recently poured out [his teaching] at night.
As for "Ink," it refers to a monk who reveals his shadow yet conceals his form. Examining this closely, neither of these two is fully realized. Why?
There is only the moon shining on the wall; there is no wind blowing through the leaves.

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Speech is slander; silence is deception. Speech and silence are the single pivot of the ultimate. Upon hearing this, even Buddhas and Patriarchs lose their courage.
Zeng Lang rolled three wooden balls; Deshan brandished his white staff. All these are merely playing with spirits and presenting reflections.
How can they compare to striking the big toe, bumping into the door, or seeing through the opening of the curtain? Only such things can truly make one a monk."
A Model. (Striking the whisk) One cry of a crane atop a thousand peaks;
on the Lantern Festival, there is rain. Master Huanxi of Tiantong ascends the hall to give thanks. Holding up his staff, he says:

"The moon upon the peak of Taibai, the lamp beneath the waters of Hanquan. Their pure light is divided above and below, yet for a thousand miles it shines with equal clarity. As for this equal clarity—
Stop! Ultimately, by what cause does the lamp’s flame arise? From where does the moon ascend? The Master struck his staff and said:
"A single drop that does not come turns into night rain; it cannot deceive the elder brother, Teacher Kāśyapa."

He thanked the assembly for the repairs to the various quarters and for the clearing of fields, then ascended the hall. Holding up his staff, he said: "The misty trees are cleared away; the morning moon hangs from the eaves.
The wooden horse neighs as the ridge clouds finish their plowing; the spring wind blows rain upon the bellowing clay ox. To realize this before a sound leaves the gap is to be without error;
together we shall enjoy the joy of Dharma and the bliss of Zen. He struck the ground with the staff. "To forge a blade, one must have the iron of Bīṇzhou."

Ascending the hall: Today is the fifteenth day of the third month; in the blink of an eye, spring draws to its close. A foot-long jade disc cannot compensate for a single inch of time; how could these bright days be spent in vain?
Piteous indeed is the cry of the cuckoo, sounding again and again; it cries until its throat bleeds, yet there is no place for its song to be used.
Fojian held up his incense and said: "Looking up at Tianwan, shouting atop Sheling; in years past, I was deceived and lost my way, like spilled water that can never be reclaimed.
To call each other 'father' and 'son' in the hall, yet to be enemies when turned away from one another—such a shadow I have no wish to see again.

Yet who would have thought we would follow one another through the realms and arrive together here in Fuzhou? No, no, no! Rest, rest, rest! This coarse incense is but a forced gathering of soil. Thus he spoke.
Breaking [precepts] does not constitute enmity.

For the summer retreat, I offer this small *chan* discourse: take the *Awakening of Faith in the Mahāyāna* (*Yuanjue*) as the monastery. With a cangue upon your head and shackles upon your feet, you mistake empty space for your true essence;
east and west are no longer distinguished, nor are north and south. Thus you pass through the long period of one hundred and twenty days.
To fuse the past, present, and future within a single thought-moment is still like a weary fish stranded in a shallow pool or a dull bird perched upon a reed.
Even if you manage to stride through the gate of Xuefeng, ascend the hall of Xuefeng, enter the chamber of Xuefeng, and perceive the person of Xuefeng—[it remains so].
"You are not yet on the Way," he said. "Do not say that the mountain terrain here is steep; ahead there is an even higher peak.
He further cited the Patriarch Zhengjue of this very mountain: "He took the entire earth and gathered it up, making it as large as a grain of rice, and tossed it before you.
The 'lacquer buckets' do not understand; beat the drum and invite everyone to look! [The Master] commented: "There is no lack of looking, but do you know?"
Is this the standing place of Xuefeng? If you can determine it with certainty, you may dwell comfortably within the mouth of a tortoise-nosed snake.
If, however, you have not yet reached this realization, feel free to guess eastward or westward as you please.

Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Throughout the lands of the ten directions, there is only the One Vehicle Dharma. What is this One Vehicle Dharma? The plum rains have passed, the lotus fragrance wafts;
a warm breeze rises from the palace pavilions, bringing a subtle coolness. Do you understand? He descended from his seat and went on a tour of the hall to drink tea.
Ascending the hall: At the break of dawn, the autumn equinox has begun; the chill has already reached the mountain peaks. As they speak of wind and talk of dew, the cicadas chirp with urgency;

as they chant by the steps and sing by the walls, the crickets’ voices drift through the air. Without engaging in deliberations on the Buddha-dharma, and without interpreting the seasonal scene, he raises his hand and says:
"The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara buys sesame cakes with money. Then, letting go of his hand, he says: "But it turns out—"

A piece of raw iron. Entering the hall: "The ninth day is the very occasion; ascending the heights, I announce it to the assembly. Yellow chrysanthemums are found everywhere—how could they be confined to the eastern hedge?
A rare sight to encounter, I pluck forth this single branch. Holding up his whisk, he says: "Do you see? Before one's eyes, no one understands."
